newsitem.title: UK: Sugar freight business slow, trickle of new orders.
newsitem.headline: Sugar freight business slow, trickle of new orders.

text.p: London's sugar freight market got off to a slow start on Monday with little reported in the way of fixtures and only a few new orders cited to keep business ticking over, shipbrokers said.
Louis Dreyfus quoted for 14,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Thailand to south Korea for May 5/10.
Shipbrokers said Lorico's recent order for 16,000 tonnes in bulk from Cuba to Alexandria for May 15/25 was still open, as was Benham's bulk order from Georgetown to US Gulf/Atlantic for May 1/15.

Secretan entered the market with a swathe of fresh inquiry, mainly for bagged sugar. It was open for 4/5,000 tonnes from Continent to Batumi for May 1/10, 13,000 from the same origin to Mediterranean for May/14 days notice and 5/6,000 from Thailand to Chittagong for prompt/seven days notice.
Of the bulk orders, Secretan quoted for 10,000 tonnes from Goa to Lisbon for May 1/7 and a 14,000-tonne cargo from Thailand to south China for April 28/May 5.
ESTC quoted on account for a timecharter, 25/38,000 dwt, for Cuba delivery and redelivery Med/Black Sea for May 1/10. It gave a voyage alternative of 24/30,000 tonnes in bulk.
Shipbrokers said Czarnikow Rionda was still open with its recent orders for Colombian and Mexican bagged sugar into Africa and Colombo.

Iran is thought to have bought four cargoes of white sugar last week for shipment between May and July, with a leading London trade house named as a seller of two FOB cargoes for May/June and another for June/July, c & f.
An Asian house was said to have sold Iran a FOB cargo of white sugar for May/June. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 8064
